item.title: Nissen Richards Studio and SP(R)INT STUDIO collaborate on permanent Gígur Visitor Centre within stunning Icelandic nature reserve by Nissen Richards Studio
item.description: Nissen Richards Studio, together with local Icelandic design partner SP(R)INT STUDIO, has created the permanent exhibition, interior and graphic design for The Gígur Visitor Centre in Iceland, along with the centre’s welcome area, café and shop. The brief for the project was to create a new permanent exhibition relating to the Mývatn nature reserve and the northern highlights of Vatnajökull National Park. item.title: Obama Presidential Center gets Juneteenth opening date
item.description: The forthcoming Obama Presidential Center in Chicago's Jackson Park now has an opening date: The Obama Foundation announced over the weekend that a dedication ceremony will take place on the John Lewis Plaza on June 18, before the campus and the museum officially open to the public on the following day, coinciding with the Juneteenth federal holiday. item.title: Jule Pond by LaGuardia Design Group
item.description: Jule Pond's architectural siting was derived from an intensive, early collaborative effort between the Landscape Architect and Architect. Due to the sensitive nature of the site—a low-lying expanse of a former farm field bordering on a freshwater pond—FEMA regulations required that the house be elevated twelve feet above grade. item.title: Hayground by LaGuardia Design Group
item.description: This project exemplifies how thoughtful landscape design can elevate both ecological stewardship and experiential quality. Its standout feature lies in the innovative terracing strategy, which transforms challenging topography into a layered sequence of outdoor rooms that feel organic rather than imposed. item.title: Unknown Works uses 'Paper-tecture' for Barbican retrospective for Beatriz González by Unknown Works
item.description: Using paper as its primary material, architects Unknown Works have designed the UK's first major retrospective exhibition for Colombian artist, curator, art historian and educator Beatriz González at the Barbican. González was born in 1932 and sadly passed away at the beginning of this year, aged 93. item.title: Silver Lake by dSPACE Studio Architecture
item.description: This rural retreat offers the homeowners a layered architectural experience that invites daily interaction with nature and their art collection. Originally from Rio, they sought to incorporate Brazilian elements into a design that harmonizes with the land. In this serene setting overlooking a rustic lake, the structure becomes a sculptural object—a contemplative space that blurs the boundary between architecture and art. item.title: The Rhombus by Yu2e, Inc.
item.description: This house occupies a leftover parcel at the end of a residential block in Silver Lake, created by the irregular intersection of streets that meet at sharp angles.
